text:
Yara: Observed a spike of 408/timeout errors from Android devices on long-tail connections. More common on older devices (API 25-28) and emulator images.
Devon: Any pattern? streaming, many short requests, or long-lived idle connections?
Yara: Mix of many short REST calls with some long-poll endpoints. Logs show TCP FIN from server but client still tries to reuse connection, then times out on next request. Happens more when app is backgrounded or device sleeps.
Oleg: Sounds like connection pool is holding stale sockets. Older Android kernels and stock HTTP stacks sometimes don't surface socket CLOSE to OkHttp quickly; next request tries to reuse a dead socket and we hit read timeouts. OkHttp usually has keep-alive/ping and health checks but defaults vary across versions.
Priya: Is this reproducible in the sample-app?
Yara: Yes. I made a small repro that sends 200 short requests, then sleeps the device, then resumes and sends 50 more. ~5% of those 50 fail with 408/read-timeout. Doesn't reproduce if we create a new OkHttpClient per resume.
Devon: Creating a new client is heavyweight. Better to make the pool evict dead connections or enable pings. What's our Android SDK default ConnectionPool?
Oleg: Our Java SDK used ConnectionPool(5, 5, TimeUnit.MINUTES) and no pingInterval. The Kotlin SDK example docs show pingInterval(15, TimeUnit.SECONDS) which means sample apps behaved differently. We have an SDK parity issue: Java vs Kotlin examples have different resilience defaults.
Priya: We should standardize defaults and document the trade-offs. Pings help detect dead HTTP/2 streams / keepalive loss but cost battery. For mobile, a longer ping interval is reasonable. Also a background-aware evictor can proactively close idle connections on app background to avoid reuse.
Yara: I prototyped a simple ConnectionPool evictor + keepalive config that fixed our repro on API 26 emulator:
```kotlin
val pool = ConnectionPool(5, 2, TimeUnit.MINUTES)
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .connectionPool(pool)
  .pingInterval(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS) // lightweight TCP/HTTP/2 pings
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(true)
  .build()

// background evictor
val evictJob = CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.Default).launch {
  while (isActive) {
    delay(TimeUnit.MINUTES.toMillis(1))
    pool.evictAll() // nudge to close stale sockets when app is backgrounded
  }
}
```
Devon: Nice. A few notes: pool.evictAll() closes all sockets, maybe too aggressive. Prefer evictIdle with a smaller window if you implement your own evictor (use reflection with care) or call client.dispatcher().executorService().purge()? But evictAll() is simplest and works for repro.
Oleg: Also highlight that .pingInterval behaves differently on HTTP/1.1 (no effect) vs HTTP/2 (settings frame pings). For some older Android system OkHttp versions pingInterval is a no-op. That's why this bug appeared more on older images.
Priya: Action items for SDK: 1) standardize examples across Java/Kotlin to include connectionPool + conservative pingInterval (30s) with note about battery tradeoffs; 2) add guidance to mobile onboarding about evicting connections on background/foreground transitions; 3) add a sample-app test that simulates sleep/resume and fails when >1% of post-resume requests error.
Devon: Also add a migration note: if your app observes rare read timeouts after device sleep, try enabling pingInterval or evicting the pool on background. Provide the code snippets.
CI-Bot: canary: scheduled sdk-0.15.0-keepalive-evict-rc1 build and sample-app test lane.
Yara: I'll push the repro and a short doc to internal sample-apps. Will file follow-up to track SDK parity fix. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
